nodes.label: QA / Browser Engineering Lead
nodes.rationale: Sole owner of the shared browser daemon because it is a single persistent Chromium session — concurrent drivers corrupt shared cookies/localStorage/tabs and produce phantom bugs; runs /qa-only rather than /qa in team mode because autonomous auto-fixing would create unmergeable conflicts across implementers editing the same repo.

nodes.label: Browser Daemon Collision Across Agents
nodes.rationale: The gstack browse daemon is one persistent Chromium session; two agents driving it concurrently corrupt session state and produce phantom bugs, so browser ownership is now exclusive to qa-browser-lead.

nodes.label: File-Ownership Map Mechanism
nodes.rationale: v1's CTO agent said 'never let two agents edit the same high-conflict files' with nothing to enforce it; v2 requires the solutions architect to emit a file-ownership map and every implementer to run /freeze <glob> first.

nodes.label: permissionMode: Not Applied At Spawn
nodes.rationale: Teammates start with the lead's permission settings; per-teammate modes cannot be set at spawn time, so v1's permission table implied a guarantee that does not exist.

nodes.label: skills: Frontmatter Ignored for Teammates
nodes.rationale: Teammates load skills and MCP servers from project/user settings, not agent frontmatter, so v1's skills: list per agent never influenced behaviour; fix moved skill guidance into agent bodies.

nodes.label: tools: Allowlist Is the One Enforced Restriction
nodes.norm_label: tools: allowlist is the one enforced restriction
nodes.rationale: v1 gave reviewers permissionMode: plan with no tool restriction, so combined with /review's auto-fix a 'read-only' reviewer could still write; v2 gives every read-only role a tools: list with no Write/Edit.

nodes.label: gbrain Semantic Search Optimisation
nodes.rationale: Every teammate starts with an empty context window and greps around to orient; semantic search pays for itself when multiple teammates orient simultaneously.

nodes.rationale: Revenue is enforced at the Edge Function level, not just hidden in the UI, so staff cannot bypass restrictions via API calls.

nodes.label: Supabase Migrations Sole-Owner Rule
nodes.rationale: Migrations are append-only and sequentially numbered; an out-of-band edit to an applied migration corrupts every environment that already ran it.

nodes.label: Five chained steps at 90% accuracy = 59% argument
nodes.norm_label: five chained steps at 90% accuracy = 59% argument
nodes.rationale: The arithmetic justification for WAT: reasoning is probabilistic and compounding error across chained steps demands moving execution into deterministic scripts (Layer 3) rather than adding more prompting (Layer 2).

nodes.label: WAT Layer 2 — Agents
nodes.rationale: Satisfied: 21 agents with explicit orchestration, error escalation, clarifying-question rules, and handoff protocol — arguably over-built relative to the other two layers.

nodes.label: WAT Layer 3 — Tools
nodes.rationale: Absent: zero .py files, no tools/ directory, no .env, no deterministic execution anywhere prior to the audit — the layer WAT's core reliability argument depends on.

nodes.label: WAT Layer 1 — Workflows
nodes.rationale: Partial: docs/MISSIONS.md and agent bodies are role/team-composition instructions, not task SOPs; no workflows/ directory with the objective→inputs→tools→outputs→edge-cases shape existed before the audit.
